From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acme.com>, Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exec sponsor mapping + EB meeting plan for ACME close

Hi Samir / Olivia —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To keep momentum toward the Q2 close, I attached an updated Mutual Action Plan (MAP-v2.xlsx) and a short EB availability calendar (EB-availability.ics). High level asks here:

- We need final names and responsibilities for ACME exec sponsors (who will present, who will sign off on security/ops, who owns procurement).
- Lock a 90–120 minute Exec Briefing (EB) where Redwood presents: run deck, eval plan, canary rollout, and contract/terms Q&A.
- Agree on the MAP milestones and owners so we can map to internal resource availability (engineering, security, legal).

Proposed EB windows (pick one):
- Option A: Tue Apr 5, 10:00–12:00 PT (internal canary + Q&A)
- Option B: Wed Apr 13, 09:00–11:00 PT (wider audience, CFO/GC invited)

If you can confirm exec sponsor names and which window works by EOD Thu (Mar 18), we’ll lock the invite, hand off the run deck to Marissa for rehearsal, and route the MAP to ACME Legal for redlines.

Attachments: [Attachment: MAP-v2.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet, 42 KB)] [Attachment: EB-availability.ics (calendar invite, 3 KB)]

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

Marcus —

Appreciate the clear plan and the MAP attachment. Quick answers from our side:

- Exec sponsors: Samir Shah (CPO) — overall sponsor and procurement owner; Olivia Grant (VP Sales) — exec champion for revenue recognition and rollout; Nicole Park (Head of InfoSec) — security point-of-contact (I copied legal but will loop Nicole once she’s back Tuesday).
- EB window: Option A (Apr 5, 10–12 PT) looks best for the core decision team. If Nicole can’t make Apr 5 we can do a follow-up session with InfoSec.

I uploaded a short availability grid to the ACME shared drive and attached a tentative calendar entry. Also put ACME Legal on copy for the MAP redline timeline.

We should confirm who from Redwood will present the architecture vs. product use cases so I can prep slides on our side.

—Samir

Nice — thanks Marcus and Samir. A couple tactical notes from the Ops side before we lock things:

1) Sponsor mapping: I sketched owner assignments inline in the MAP (column: "EB owner"). Recommend the following split:
   - Product/Use Cases: Marcus (present lead) + Marissa (customer stories)
   - Architecture/Scale & Security: Karthik (deep dive) + Monica (runtime constraints)
   - Commercial/Terms: Marissa + Legal (ACME)

2) Evaluation plan: suggest a two-stage plan in the EB:
   - Stage 1 (Canary eval): short production-like run with 1–2 endpoints and 2–3 critical prompts (30–60 minutes) to surface integration questions.
   - Stage 2 (Acceptance run): multi-hour throughput/latency baseline + data flow validation (follow-up with InfoSec).

3) Schedule refinement: if ACME confirms Apr 5 for the core EB, let's reserve Apr 6 as a morning buffer for the canary run (engineering standby). If InfoSec needs more time, we can schedule Nicole’s security deep dive on Apr 12.

I attached a one-page checklist (in MAP) that maps each milestone to a Redwood owner and estimated hours. Marissa — can you take the lead on the run deck + rehearsal slots?

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solution Engineering | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

All —

Confirmed: Apr 5, 10:00–12:00 PT is locked for the Exec Briefing. I created the invite and included the attached run deck outline (first pass) and rehearsal times. Action items from here:

- Marissa (me): finalize run deck, schedule two rehearsals (Apr 1 & Apr 3), coordinate demo data fingerprinting with Monica.
- Marcus: send final list of attendees and who will present (I assigned roles in the invite).
- Karthik / Monica: engineering on-call Apr 5–6 for the canary run; prepare the short canary test plan and threshold metrics (latency, error rate, token cost estimate).
- ACME Legal: please expect MAP redline requests by Mar 19; Karthik and I will be available for quick calls.

I’ll circulate the rehearsal calendar and a short checklist (10 bullets) for the EB. If anything changes on ACME side (Nicole or legal timing), we’ll keep the buffer Apr 12 free for the deeper security review.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to a tight run.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
